user_input: I finally got my 9.2 CGPA and cleared the Amazon coding round, but I came back to my hostel room, looked at the wall, and felt completely empty. If this is the peak of what I’ve been killing myself for since 11th grade, why does it feel so hollow? I keep thinking about working 10 hours a day just to buy things I don't need until I die, and it makes me want to just stop breathing.

I was sitting up at 3 AM trying to debug my compiler design lab code, and I just looked out the window and got hit by this massive wave of dread. We’re on this tiny rock spinning in a silent, freezing void of nothingness, and I'm supposed to care about syntax errors and whether I make 12 LPA or 24 LPA? It feels like we are all playing this absurd, fake game to distract ourselves from how terrifyingly insignificant we are.

I look at the alumni updates on LinkedIn—all these people posting about 'excited to start my journey as an Associate Analyst'—and I feel this physical sickness in my stomach. Is this really the rest of my life? Just commuting, writing code for some insurance company, staring at a screen, sleeping, and repeating it for forty years? I feel like I'm marching toward my own execution and everyone around me is celebrating it.

Every single day is identical. I wake up, attend lectures I don’t care about, work on projects I hate, scroll my phone, and go to sleep. I feel like a ghost haunting my own life. I’m only 21 but I feel like I've already died inside, and there’s no point to any of this because nothing I do actually matters to anyone, not even to me.

I chose CS because my parents said it would secure my future, but now I’m in my third year with three backlogs, struggling to write a basic sorting algorithm, and I hate it. But the worst part is, even if I quit and did what I thought I wanted—like literature—I feel like I’d still end up miserable and broke anyway. It feels like every door leads to the same dark room, and I’m just wasting my youth choosing which wall to hit my head against.

Just finished a 6-hour DSA coding sprint and got all test cases to pass, but instead of feeling happy, I just stared at my monitor and felt this cold, empty pit in my stomach. What is actually the point of this? I'm grinding 14 hours a day to get a 12 LPA job to pay off loans, buy things I don't need, and then just die. My parents are constantly sending screenshots of relatives' kids getting 30+ LPA packages, and I just feel like a nameless cog in a machine that doesn't care if I live or die. Does this hollow feeling ever go away, or is this just what 'success' is supposed to feel like?

I look at the graduation checklist and my 9.2 CGPA and I feel absolutely nothing. We're all just aggressively optimizing our resumes, doing fake networking on LinkedIn, and pretending we care about 'synergy' and 'deliverables' when we're actually just terrified of being left behind. I woke up at 3 AM last night sweating because I suddenly realized that even if I land my dream role at a FAANG company, I am still just a tiny speck on a wet rock floating in an infinite, silent universe. How are my peers so unfazed by how utterly meaningless all of this is?

It’s 4 AM and I’m staring at my DBMS and OS notes for the midterms tomorrow, and I just started crying because none of this matters. We are born, we memorize schemas, we write queries, we get a desk job, we get old, and we die. My roommate is asleep, probably dreaming about his upcoming Amazon internship, and I’m sitting here wondering why I even exist if my entire life is just a series of administrative hurdles designed to test my compliance. I don’t want to fail my midterms, but I also don’t want to spend my life pretending this trivial stuff is the pinnacle of human existence.

Ever since the placement drive started, I feel like I've been wearing a mask that's suffocating me. I had to pitch myself to three different HR reps today as 'highly motivated and passionate about cloud infrastructure' when in reality, I don't give a single damn about cloud infrastructure. I came back to my hostel room, locked the door, and just sat on the floor feeling this profound, terrifying sense of alienation. If I have to spend the next forty years lying about who I am just to secure a basic living, I don't know how I'm going to survive.

I turned twenty last week and instead of celebrating, I spent the whole night crying in the bathroom. The realization that my childhood is dead and I'm being shoved onto this high-speed conveyor belt toward corporate slavery is terrifying. I look at the adults around me—always tired, talking about interest rates and housing prices, completely devoid of any spark—and I feel this crushing existential dread that my future is just a slow death of my creativity. Is this really all there is, or is there a way to grow up without losing your soul?

I just got my results for the 5th sem. 9.4 CGPA. I spent the last three months locked in my room doing DSA questions on LeetCode and ignoring everyone. My dad is already talking about the 20 LPA package his friend's son got. But I looked at my transcript today and felt absolutely nothing. Just this cold, terrifying realization that even if I land that corporate job, I’m just going to be doing this same meaningless loop until I die. Why does everyone run this race so happily when it leads to nowhere?

Everyone in my hostel is prepping for placements. They're updating LinkedIn, sharing resume templates, and crying about coding rounds. I'm sitting here looking at my screen, and I feel completely detached, like I'm watching a movie of someone else's life. Is this it? We study for 18 years just to sit in a cubicle and optimize database queries for some fintech giant? I feel like a ghost walking through campus. I don't want to fail, but I don't want this 'success' either.

I turned 21 yesterday and spent the night staring at my ceiling. My friends threw a party, we had cake, but inside I was just screaming. Time is moving so fast and I have absolutely no anchor. I look at the stars and feel so utterly small and insignificant, like my entire existence is just a brief, painful spark that doesn't matter to the universe at all. Everyone is congratulating me, but I went to the washroom and just stared at the mirror feeling completely numb. I spent four years grinding DSA, keeping my CGPA at 9.2, skipping trips, and for what? This hollow, dead feeling in my chest? If the 'prize' at the end of this brutal race feels this meaningless, what is even the point of the next forty years?

It's 3 AM, my desk is covered in half-finished compiler design notes, and I’m just staring at the ceiling fan spinning. It hit me that in a hundred years, literally nobody will care about my GPA, my backlogs, or whether I made it to a FAANG company. We are just tiny, accidental specks of dust floating on a rock in the middle of a cold, silent universe, yet I'm sitting here crying over a stupid coding lab evaluation tomorrow. How do people just ignore this massive, terrifying emptiness and pretend like these daily chores actually matter?

I’m graduating in two months and everyone is posting their farewell videos, emotional bios, and 'excited to announce' updates on LinkedIn. I feel like an absolute ghost walking through campus. I look at my friends who have their entire lives mapped out—masters in the US, consulting gigs, startups—and I feel this deep, paralyzing terror of the sheer passage of time. I don't want to step into the 'real world' because it feels like a giant, mechanical grinder that eats your youth and spits out a burnt-out corporate drone.

My dad forced me into computer science because of the 'scope,' and now I spend twelve hours a day in front of a screen debugging code I despise. I had a panic attack in the library today not because the lab was hard, but because I realized this is it—this is my life now. Wake up, stare at a screen, write code for some faceless corporation, get paid, buy stuff, grow old, and die. I feel so alienated from my own hands, like I'm playing a video game of someone else’s incredibly boring life.

I turned twenty-one over the semester break, and instead of celebrating, I spent the whole day locked in my room crying. When did time start moving so fast? I feel like I was just a kid riding my bicycle around my neighborhood, and suddenly I have a CGPA to maintain, taxes to learn, and an impending sense of decay. It feels like every door of possibility is slamming shut one by one, leaving me trapped in this mediocre version of myself that I never even chose to be.

I just got the confirmation for the final round of this 25 LPA product company, and my dad is already telling all our relatives. But I went to the washroom, locked the door, and just stared at the tiles. I don't feel happy. I feel this terrifying, cold numbness inside. Like, okay, I get this job, then I work 14 hours a day writing APIs, buy a car, get old, and die. Is this seriously the whole point of existing? It feels like a massive, pointless trap and I can't breathe.

Just finished my 5th-semester midterms. Got a 9.2 CGPA and my DSA lab manual is spotless. But tonight, I’m looking at the ceiling fan spin and feeling this sheer, raw terror. We are just tiny specs of dust spinning on a wet rock in the middle of nowhere, and I'm losing sleep over whether I used the right sorting algorithm. It makes me feel so ridiculously insignificant that I just want to stop trying altogether.

Every single time I open LinkedIn, there's another 'I'm pleased to share' post with people landing summer internships. I have two backlogs in math, and I'm sitting here in my messy hostel room eating cold noodles. It’s not even just about the placements anymore—I look at this endless cycle of high school, college, corporate rat race, retirement, and death. Why are we all pretending this is some beautiful journey when it feels like a slow-motion march to the grave?

I'm graduating in two months. Everyone is talking about moving to Bangalore, renting flats, and choosing between 401ks. I feel like I'm playing a character in a movie I didn't audition for. I look in the mirror and don't recognize the person wearing the graduation gown. I’m terrified of waking up at 40 and realizing I lived a completely hollow life just to please my parents and society. Is this all adulting is? Just choosing your favorite flavor of slow death?

My mom keeps sending me screenshots of my cousin’s onsite placement in Germany, talking about 'settling down'. I look at my syllabus, my pending minor project, my crumbling mental health, and I feel nothing but existential dread. Even if I do everything right—get the branch change, clear the tech rounds, move abroad—I’m still just running on a hamster wheel designed by someone else. I feel so utterly trapped in this timeline, and the worst part is I don't even know what I would choose if I had a choice.

I just cleared my Amazon round 2, and my flatmates are celebrating outside. I’m locked in my room staring at the ceiling fan, feeling this crushing, empty dread. What am I actually running for? If I get this 30 LPA package, I'll just sit in a cubicle writing API endpoints until I die. I don't feel happy, I just feel numb and terrified of how meaningless it all is.

It's 3 AM during semester break and everyone's asleep. My dad left a brochure for GATE prep on my desk, but I went to the balcony and looked at the sky and just started shivering. We are literally monkeys on a wet rock spinning in empty space, and I'm supposed to care about whether I choose WebDev or System Design? This whole life setup feels like a collective delusion and I'm suffocating.

My CGPA dropped to 7.2 after the DSA labs and everyone on my feed is posting about their summer internships. But honestly? I don't even care about the grade, I'm just terrified that there's no actual 'me' inside this body. I’ve just been following instructions my whole life to survive, and now that I have to choose a path, I look inside and find absolutely nothing. It's like I'm a ghost walking through college.

Next month is graduation and my mom is already talking about me moving to Bangalore for the software engineer role. I feel this cold, heavy brick in my stomach because I realize this is it—the end of my youth. Now it's just 40 years of 9-to-5, paying bills, and pretending to care about sprint planning until I get old and die. Why is everyone else so eager to jump into this meat grinder?

Got my midterms back and I did fine, but during dinner my dad started comparing my cousin’s 45 LPA package at Atlassian with what I might get. I looked at his face, all stressed and intense over numbers, and I just wanted to scream. Why do we spend our tiny, beautiful, temporary lives competing over imaginary points? I feel so alien and disconnected from my own family, like I'm speaking a language they can't even hear.

I cracked my placements, got the 12 LPA package everyone was killing themselves for, and my parents are flexing it on family WhatsApp groups. But I sat down at my desk last night, looked at the contract, and just felt this cold, heavy numbness. What was the point of sacrificing my sleep, grinding LeetCode daily, and crying over semester GPAs if this victory feels like absolutely nothing? I feel like I'm climbing a ladder that's leaning against the completely wrong wall, and the sheer emptiness of the next 40 years of corporate grind is terrifying me.

I’m in my third year of BTech and my CGPA just dropped to 6.8 after the midterms. My roommate is sorting out his MS applications, my childhood friend just bought a car from his startup equity, and here I am, staring at a DSA lab sheet, unable to understand a single line of graph theory. The universe feels so massive, and my existence feels like a tiny, insignificant error code that will eventually just get deleted. If my entire worth is tied to whether I can optimize a search algorithm or clear a backlog, why am I even participating in this absurd, exhausting race?

Everyone keeps asking me what I want to do after graduation, and I just freeze. I look at my peers who have their 5-year plans perfectly mapped out, and then I look at myself—I don't even know what brings me joy anymore because I've spent my whole youth just surviving exams. The thought of picking a career pathway feels like choosing which cage I want to be locked in for the rest of my life. I'm terrified that whatever path I choose, I'll wake up at 40, full of regret, realizing I wasted my one shot at being alive on something I hated.

I turned twenty-one yesterday, and instead of celebrating, I spent the night crying on the bathroom floor. I feel this crushing adulting dread that I'm running out of time, but I don't even know what I'm running toward. My parents keep talking about my 'bright future' and 'packages,' but all I can think about is how every single day is exactly the same—wake up, attend lectures I don't care about, study to pass, sleep, repeat. Is this all life is? Just a series of endless, mundane routines until we grow old and die?

I used to be so passionate about writing and painting when I was in high school, but I chose engineering because 'it's safe.' Now, I look at myself in the mirror and I don't even recognize the person staring back—I feel like a ghost inhabiting a body that only exists to debug code. I have zero energy left to create anything beautiful anymore, and I'm gripped by this terrifying feeling that I've permanently traded my soul for survival. What if the creative, vibrant version of me is dead, and I'm just a shell waiting for the corporate world to consume the rest of me?

I just finished my DSA coding lab and got a perfect score, but I sat in the washroom for twenty minutes after, staring at the tiled floor, feeling absolutely nothing. My dad keeps texting me about 'dream packages' and 40 LPA placement stats at my college, but when I look at these seniors who got those offers, they look like zombies. What are we actually doing? If the grand prize for surviving this hell is 14 hours a day of writing APIs for a fintech startup, why am I even waking up for 8 AM classes?

Everyone is talking about their career roadmap, and I’m just staring at my 8.9 CGPA feeling like a complete fraud because I don't care about any of it. Sometimes I look out the window of my hostel room at 3 AM and think about how tiny our campus is, how tiny our city is, and how we are just microscopic dust floating on a rock in space. If nothing we do actually matters in the grand scheme of the universe, why does getting a C in Microprocessors feel like the end of the world?

I’m in my final year and the placement season just started, but I feel this terrifying, hollow panic every time I open LinkedIn. I see these alumni posting about 'humbled and honored to join...' and I just want to scream because it feels like a cult where everyone pretends to be happy about selling their souls. I feel so alone in this—like if I don't jump into this meat grinder, I'll starve, but if I do, I'll lose whatever is left of my actual self.

My parents spent their life savings to send me to this engineering college, and I have three backlogs in my third semester. I look at the marksheet and I don't even feel sad anymore, just this weird, cold detachment, like I'm watching someone else ruin their life. I’m sitting in the back of the lecture hall right now while the professor drones on about Fourier transforms, and I'm just wondering... if I disappear tomorrow, does the universe even hiccup? The sheer pointlessness of trying to fix my GPA is paralyzing.

I turned twenty-one yesterday and spent the whole night crying in the common room because the passage of time feels like a slow-motion car crash. Everyone is talking about 'adulting' and getting financial independence, but I feel like an absolute child playing dress-up in a world that demands I become a production unit. I don't want to optimize my resume, I don't want to network, I just want to understand why we are forced to build a life we never asked to be born into.
